title: Origine Eco-condos de la Pointe-aux-Lièvres
code_edition: Québec Construction Code in force at project start in 2014 (edition unstated); RBQ 2015 guide for mass-timber buildings up to 12 storeys is cited
document_date: Unknown; the project case study describes the 2014 project start and 2016-2017 construction

facts.text: The French case study says the code's acceptable solutions at project start in 2014 required a building above four storeys to use noncombustible construction, leading the design team to seek equivalent measures from the RBQ.
It states that the RBQ accepted the equivalent-measures request and later recorded many measures in its 2015 guide for mass-timber buildings up to 12 storeys.
The study describes a 12-storey timber structure and fire-resistance design work involving complete wall/floor assemblies, connections and penetrations.
The report describes CAN/ULC-S101 fire-resistance testing and CAN/ULC-S115 joint/penetration testing, with a 1-hour char-design plus gypsum encapsulation strategy for a 2-hour structural rating.

limitations: Primary case study is in French; facts in this record are translated summaries.
The fire-rehabilitation report supplies a later sprinkler-activation case reference, not an approval record.
No original RBQ submission, approval letter, full laboratory test reports or permit drawings were located.
